# API and UX Requirements Checklist: Book Library Management System

**Purpose**: Review the clarity, completeness, consistency, and testability of API and user-experience requirements
**Created**: 2026-11-07
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Are create, read, update, and delete requirements defined consistently for books and members, including individual and paginated collection views? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001–FR-003]
- [x] CHK002 Are librarian access requirements specified for every catalog, member, and loan read and mutation, with these operations restricted to signed-in librarians? [Coverage, Spec §FR-018]
- [x] CHK003 Are the issue and return contracts defined with the required identifiers, due/return dates, resulting states, and atomic cross-record effects? [Completeness, Spec §FR-005–FR-008]
- [x] CHK004 Are list response requirements clear about pagination metadata, retained filters, and stable ordering? [Completeness, Spec §FR-013]
- [ ] CHK005 Are API responses and user-facing requirements defined for loading, validation, authorization, missing-record, conflict, and unexpected-server-error states? [Gap, Spec §FR-014–FR-015]

## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK006 Are API error conditions mapped unambiguously to HTTP status codes, especially invalid input, unavailable books, duplicates, missing records, and unexpected failures? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-004, FR-007, FR-015]
- [x] CHK007 Are search matching rules, filter combination behavior, sort choices, direction, and tie-breaking clearly defined across the specification and API contract? [Clarity, Spec §FR-011–FR-013]
- [ ] CHK008 Are the pagination defaults, maximum page size, invalid-page behavior, and out-of-range-page behavior explicit and consistent? [Clarity, Spec §FR-013; Assumptions]
- [x] CHK009 Is the due-date boundary clear about the exact issue instant, library-local date, and when a loan changes from active to overdue? [Clarity, Spec §FR-006, FR-010; Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK010 Are category naming and matching rules clear enough to prevent inconsistent filtering across book creation, updates, and catalog search? [Gap, Spec §FR-001, FR-012]

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK011 Are desktop-only interface requirements and the exclusion of mobile-specific layouts stated consistently across functional requirements, success criteria, and assumptions? [Consistency, Spec §FR-016, SC-004; Assumptions]
- [x] CHK012 Are authentication requirements consistent between the specification's librarian sign-in policy and the plan's session, sign-out, and request-protection expectations? [Consistency, Spec §FR-018; Plan §Design Decisions]
- [x] CHK013 Are duplicate ISBN/email handling and conflict responses consistent between the specification, data model, and API contract? [Consistency, Spec §FR-004; Data Model §Book, §Member]
- [ ] CHK014 Are deletion, archival, and historical-loan retention requirements consistent across the user scenarios, functional requirements, data model, and API contract? [Consistency, Spec §FR-009; Data Model §Book, §Member, §Loan]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK015 Is the two-second search outcome defined with an unambiguous start/end measurement point and representative query/filter mix? [Measurability, Spec §SC-003]
- [x] CHK016 Are the concurrency acceptance criteria precise about simultaneous issue attempts and the consistency of book, loan, and member-count outcomes? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001–SC-002]
- [ ] CHK017 Is the evidence required to determine WCAG 2.2 Level AA conformance for all in-scope workflows clearly identified? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §FR-019, SC-007]
- [x] CHK018 Is the desktop viewport acceptance criterion objectively assessable without implying mobile layout support? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §FR-016, SC-004]

## Scenario and Edge Case Coverage

- [x] CHK019 Are sign-in failure, expired session, sign-out, and unauthorized access scenarios specified for librarian-only data and actions? [Gap, Spec §FR-018]
- [ ] CHK020 Are API and user-facing requirements defined for concurrent edits, retries, and transaction failures without allowing a partial issue or return? [Coverage, Spec §FR-006–FR-009]
- [x] CHK021 Are user-facing recovery paths defined when a request fails after the user submits a book, member, issue, or return form? [Gap, Spec §FR-015]
- [ ] CHK022 Are empty, loading, and filtered-to-no-results states distinguished for catalog, member, active-loan, and overdue views? [Coverage, Spec §FR-014]

## Dependencies and Assumptions

- [x] CHK023 Are the required operating assumptions for librarian account provisioning and initial access documented well enough to avoid an unspecified sign-in setup flow? [Dependency, Spec §FR-018; Plan §Design Decisions]
- [x] CHK024 Are the library time zone and transaction-capable database requirements explicit as prerequisites for the due-date and atomicity guarantees? [Dependency, Spec §FR-006, FR-010; Plan §Technical Context]

## Notes

- Focus selected: API contracts/data integrity and user experience/accessibility.
- Depth: Standard. Audience: feature author/reviewer.
- Mobile-specific layouts and mobile viewport support are explicitly excluded; desktop usability remains in scope.
- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation.
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers.
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`.
- Add findings inline and link to relevant specification sections.
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy review.
